meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не торопись, сначала надо всё обсудить.
examples.trans: Do not hurry, first we need to discuss everything.
These are all my people.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Quickly take this champagne away from here.
Come on, get up quickly and get dressed.
Please, just disappear from here quickly.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calmed down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.trans: Well, have you calmed down?
Calm down, please!
Calm down, everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'both', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You are both owners of this restaurant.
That is it, both of you calm down quickly.
You both leave here right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When love leaves, emptiness remains.
And besides, you are simply a pig.
What is wrong with you today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как же ты меня уже достала!
examples.trans: How sick and tired I am of you already!
I have already understood everything perfectly.
Maxim, you are already a grown boy.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: A wonderful name, allow me to treat you.
I have already understood everything perfectly.
Alright, I understand you perfectly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.

examples.text: Что тебе нужно, отстань от меня, поняла?
examples.trans: What do you want, leave me alone, understand?
I have already understood everything perfectly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is wrong with you today?

examples.text: Отстань от меня, что ты ко мне пристала?
examples.trans: Leave me alone, why are you pestering me?

examples.text: Никогда не думал, что скажу эту фразу.
examples.trans: I never thought I would say this phrase.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'specifically', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, what exactly did you understand?
Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А в клубе ты был смелее.
examples.trans: At the club you were bolder.
And besides, you are simply a pig.
You started choosing other girls.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: У моего друга завтра здесь юбилей.
examples.trans: My friend has an anniversary here tomorrow.

examples.text: Между прочим, это у меня завтра важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: By the way, I am the one who has an important event tomorrow.

examples.text: У тебя завтра ничего здесь не будет.
examples.trans: You will have nothing here tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You started choosing other girls.
Tell me, what needs to be signed there?
Sasha, bring us some good champagne.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'event' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Между прочим, это у меня завтра важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: By the way, I am the one who has an important event tomorrow.

examples.text: Витя, меня завтра на мероприятии не будет.
examples.trans: Vitya, I will not be at the event tomorrow.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, у меня здесь важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: Hello, I have an important event here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.

examples.text: У неё нет таких волос, как у меня.
examples.trans: She does not have hair like mine.

examples.text: Отстань от меня, что ты ко мне пристала?
examples.trans: Leave me alone, why are you pestering me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Я просто очень хочу быть с тобой.
examples.trans: I simply want very much to be with you.
I simply want to be with you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: You are welcome, always glad to help.

examples.text: Ты, пожалуйста, сам проследи за всем.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'yourself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Я должен часами ждать тебя там?
examples.trans: Am I supposed to wait for you there for hours?

examples.text: Ты, пожалуйста, сам проследи за всем.
examples.trans: Please watch over everything yourself.

meanings.en: to keep an eye on, to make sure
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'следить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make sure / watch over', paired with 'следить'.

examples.text: Ты, пожалуйста, сам проследи за всем.
examples.trans: Please watch over everything yourself.
We'll keep an eye on it.
I'll keep an eye on the children.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Если это угроза, она будет дорого вам стоить.
examples.trans: If that is a threat, it will cost you dearly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты вчера своим виски весь пол залил.
examples.trans: Yesterday you spilled your whiskey all over the floor.

examples.text: Витя, мы не можем провести два банкета вместе.
examples.trans: Vitya, we cannot hold two banquets together.

examples.text: У меня там гости весёлую музыку просят.
examples.trans: My guests over there are asking for cheerful music.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I never thought I would say this phrase.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сокий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('highest').

examples.trans: He has a high temperature.
This is a tall building.
He developed a high temperature.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ровень'). Common masculine noun meaning 'level' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's not my level.
What level are you?

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, or almost no one.
Listen, let us go to the bathroom quickly.

examples.text: Ты же мне продаёшь половину ресторана.
examples.trans: After all, you are selling me half of the restaurant.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.text: Немедленно шпинат убрать из нашего меню.
examples.trans: Immediately remove the spinach from our menu.

examples.text: Ну тогда я беру его обратно.
examples.trans: Well then I am taking him back.

examples.text: Почему мы вынуждены терпеть это безобразие?
examples.trans: Why are we forced to endure this outrage?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.trans: Listen, let us go to the bathroom quickly.
We will meet at work soon.
One more rude insult like that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'оплата'). Common feminine noun meaning 'advance payment / deposit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Well that is all, take the advance payment quickly.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть предоплата.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always advance payment.

examples.text: Мы же с тобой договаривались, да?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Well why, leave it here.
Why did she leave so pleased?

examples.text: Это ещё почему, гости же замёрзли.
examples.trans: Why is that, the guests got cold.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если это угроза, она будет дорого вам стоить.
examples.trans: If that is a threat, it will cost you dearly.

examples.text: Она у нас новое меню требовала.
examples.trans: She demanded a new menu from us.
Why did she leave so pleased?

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, walked away', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: Hello, dear Dmitry Vladimirovich.
Hello, do you wish for anything right now?

examples.text: Здравствуйте, у меня здесь важное мероприятие.
examples.trans: Hello, I have an important event here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('so').

examples.text: У неё нет таких волос, как у меня.
examples.trans: She does not have hair like mine.
That way you will gradually forget her.

examples.text: Я не хочу, чтобы он тебя видел здесь в таком виде.
examples.trans: I do not want him to see you here in this state.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'вольный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleased / satisfied').

examples.trans: Why did she leave so pleased?

examples.text: Гости все мокрые, они недовольны, что делать?
examples.trans: The guests are all wet, they are unhappy, what should we do?
Well, happy now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No one can fill it.
Well, or almost no one.
Well then, dear Victoria Sergeyevna.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.text: Как я вообще могла в тебя влюбиться?
examples.trans: How could I ever fall in love with you at all?
Who understands her there at all?

examples.text: Нам вообще обещали весь этот ресторан.
examples.trans: We were promised this entire restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell me, what needs to be signed there?
What are you going to manage there?
Someone is ringing the doorbell there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understands', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: Who understands her there at all?
Alright, I understand you perfectly.

examples.text: Хочу, чтобы был только я, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want it to be only me, do you understand?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'anniversary / jubilee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У моего друга завтра здесь юбилей.
examples.trans: My friend has an anniversary here tomorrow.

examples.text: Завтра будет юбилей у моего друга.
examples.trans: Tomorrow will be my friend's anniversary.

examples.text: За тебя, дорогой друг, с юбилеем!
examples.trans: To you, dear friend, happy anniversary!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maxim, you are fired, go home.
Where's my toy car?
That's mine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You started choosing other girls.

examples.text: Спасибо, друг, ты мне всё понятно объяснил.
examples.trans: Thank you, friend, you explained everything clearly to me.
Meet my friend Masha.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Ты же сама не захотела быть со мной.
examples.trans: After all, you yourself did not want to be with me.

examples.text: Хотел сказать тебе большое спасибо за всё.
examples.trans: I wanted to say thank you very much for everything.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be nervous, to fret', paired with 'разнервничаться'.

related.gloss: not to to be nervous (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Хочу, чтобы я завтра не нервничал.
examples.trans: I want not to be nervous tomorrow.
I'm nervous too!
Don't be nervous, everything is fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We will do everything at the highest level.

examples.text: Я обещал и я всё сделал, а где Витя?
examples.trans: I promised and I did everything, and where is Vitya?
We've done a lot.
